notes: THE PRIMARY OCCURRENCE, and the only one of the four in indexed, linked, published copy: the file sits at the repository root, is listed in sitemap.xml, and is linked from research-index.html and exhibits.html. claim: The prose immediately above the pull quote on the published page states the same subject in hedged, attributive form: "There is no destruction layer at Mohenjo-daro or Harappa. The collapse is associated with hydrological change - the Ghaggar-Hakra system drying, monsoon shifts - not with an attack."
notes: NOT REGISTERED AS A BREACH OF THE SAME KIND, and the contrast is the point. "Is associated with" is attributive, the causes are plural, and no single driver is named. Eleven words later the pull quote says "fell to a river". The page holds both standards and gives the weaker one display type. Logged as an internal contradiction at IC-F-001 and as the second limb of BF-028. Two things this row does not settle, because this unit retrieved no archaeological or palaeoclimate source: whether drying (a river failing) and "fell to a river" (a river acting) are the same mechanism, and whether the Ghaggar-Hakra system named here bears on Mohenjo-daro, which stands on the Indus in Sindh. Both are questions for the audit, not findings against the page.

claim: The chronology table on the published page sets "Mature Harappan urbanism ... c. 2600-1900 BCE" and "Rigveda family books composed ... c. 1500-1200 BCE" in adjacent rows of one undifferentiated column, with no source given for either and no mark of evidentiary class.
notes: THE PREMISE THE NEGATIVE IDENTIFICATION RESTS ON, and the reason BF-027 is a method failure rather than a wording complaint. The first range is excavated and radiocarbon-anchored; the second is a philological inference and is the subject of constitution section 4A, an unrun domain. The page differences them to get "three to four centuries" and publishes the difference as a rule-out. No source is cited on the page for the c. 1500-1200 BCE date, and NO ROW IN 03-REGISTERS/ ASSERTS A DATE FOR THE RIGVEDA AT ANY STATUS - checked across every register in this repository. The load-bearing figure of the page is unregistered here and unsourced there.

claim: The published page restates the negative identification in body prose: "Whatever was being stormed was in Indus country - but it was not the Indus cities."
notes: SIMILAR CLAIM, same page. Carries the first breach (BF-027) and not the second - no cause of decline is asserted. The surrounding sentence is markedly more careful than the pull quote: it concedes the geography ("the instinct that these forts sit in Indus country is geographically right", :431), states the residual positively rather than by subtraction, and the paragraph closes "No specific site has been identified with any named fort, and this platform does not name one." Recorded so that any later repair keeps what is already right here.

claim: The candidate table on the published page rules out one candidate on an absence: "Mature Harappan cities | The size fits | Ruled out by three to four centuries and by the absence of destruction layers."
notes: SIMILAR CLAIM, and a THIRD method issue this unit did not go looking for. "The absence of destruction layers" is an argument from absence used to rule out, and it is untyped: constitution section 6 requires what evidence should exist, where, probability of production, probability of survival, excavation coverage, accessibility, and ability to recognise it, before the absence is classified as NOT PRODUCED, NOT PRESERVED, NOT EXCAVATED, NOT PUBLISHED, NOT ACCESSIBLE, NOT RECOGNIZED, DOCUMENTED DESTRUCTION or ABSENT DESPITE ADEQUATE SEARCH. None of that is on the page. The same untyped absence appears at :417 and :432. Registered, not resolved; queued as RA-025.

claim: The live page what-survived-the-archive.html states a cause of Harappan decline as settled inside a subordinate clause: "Speleothems, lake cores, pollen. The Ghaggar-Hakra drying and the monsoon shift that ends Harappan urbanism are climate data, not archaeology".
notes: SIMILAR CLAIM ON ANOTHER LIVE PAGE, carrying the second breach (BF-028) only. "that ends Harappan urbanism" is a restrictive relative clause: it does not argue the causal claim, it presupposes it, which is a stronger move than asserting it and a harder one for a reader to see. Milder than MDO-001 in prominence - a table cell, not a pull quote - and identical in kind. The sentence's own subject is the separation of evidence classes, so the row is otherwise doing method-step-4 work correctly.

claim: The live page vedic-ritual-economy.html states the same subject correctly hedged: "Indus urbanism declines from c. 1900 BCE; steppe-related ancestry enters South Asia c. 2000-1500 BCE; the best current evidence points to hydrological and climatic causes for the urban collapse, with no destruction layer at the major sites."
locator: melakeela/site @79efd74, vedic-ritual-economy.html:324-328, section "Two things this page will not say"
notes: CONTROL OCCURRENCE - NOT A BREACH, and registered because a survey that recorded only failures would misdescribe the site. Same claim, four differences that matter: the evidence is attributed ("the best current evidence points to"), the causes are plural and unranked, the state of knowledge is dated ("current"), and the page states the claim as a LIMIT ON ITSELF rather than as a conclusion, under the heading "Two things this page will not say", adding "Saying otherwise is refutable". This is the house standard for the claim and BF-028's future_control names it as such. It is also evidence for BF-028's reading: the site is capable of the careful formulation and published the careless one in larger type on a different page.
